Ce(NO3)3 solution was smoothly sprayed into MoO2 powders by the conventional solid-liquid spraying processing
MoO2–Ce(NO3)3 mixture powders were then dried and reduced into metallic Mo–Ce powders by dry hydrogen in a six-heating-zones tube furnace at 850 to 950 °C
Mo–Ce powders were compacted by the cold isostatic pressing machine at 200 MPa for 10 min
sintered by the appropriate heating programs in the medium-frequency induction hydrogen furnace at 1900 °C for 28.5 h
the as-sintered 17-mm diameter Mo–Ce alloy rods were hot-drawn into 1.8 and 0.18-mm diameter wires
